title: KMS access governance and audit pipeline design notes
content:
Purpose

This note collects design decisions and operational patterns for KMS access governance, RBAC v2 integration, audit log schema, evidence automation for forensics, and SIEM ingestion mapping. Goal: produce an implementable pipeline that makes key access provenance auditable, supports BYOK/HSM flows, and provides timely alerts for suspicious key activity while preserving privacy and performance for production traffic.

Scope

- Key classes: tenant customer-managed keys (BYOK), platform-managed keys, HSM-wrapped root keys, ephemeral request keys used by inference runtime.
- Integrations: RBAC v2 entitlement system, KMS (cloud-managed + HSM appliance), audit-log pipeline, SIEM (ECS-compatible), retention and evidence archival system.

Background and constraints

- We operate across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments; design must work for cloud KMS and on-prem HSMs.
- Low-latency inference paths require minimal per-request cryptographic overhead. Audit metadata should capture access decisions and provenance without adding contention to hot paths.
- Regulatory requirements: retain cryptographic access logs for at least 3 years for enterprise customers opting into compliance add-on; retain high-fidelity forensic artifacts for 90 days for platform incidents.

High-level model: access provenance first-class

1) Principal identity: RBAC v2 issues short-lived principal tokens that include role bindings and region/tenant claims. 2) KMS access decision: KMS enforces policy; it must log decision outcome and token reference. 3) Envelope metadata: every envelope encryption/decryption operation emits a lightweight audit record with request id, principal id hash, key id, operation, justification tag, and latency. 4) Evidence bundle: on-demand or periodic archival of signed manifests + key metadata for forensic reconstruction.

RBAC v2 integration patterns

- Role to key binding table: maintain canonical mapping in the security control plane: role -> allowed key actions (wrap/unwrap, decrypt, generate). Changes go through audited PR flow.
- Attribute-based checks: use attributes (tenant_id, environment, model_family) passed as claims in principal tokens. KMS validates attribute constraints before allowing key use.
- Ephemeral delegation: for high-throughput inference, runtime requests a short-lived key-wrapping token from the control plane which the KMS accepts as delegation; delegation issuance is logged and policy-scoped.
- Escalation and Justification: CLI/API actions that request long-lived key access must include a justification token and optionally an approval id; log both.

Audit log schema (single flat event record)

We standardize on one audit event type for KMS operations to simplify ingestion. Field names below are ECS-friendly, but keys are lower_snake_case to match existing pipeline parsers. All fields are strings unless noted.

- event_type: kms_operation
- timestamp: ISO-8601 UTC
- event_id: uuid
- outcome: success | failure | denied
- principal_id: <stable-principal-id> (we store hash in SIEM; full id retained in evidence store)
- principal_token_kid: token key id (for tracing token version)
- principal_attributes: comma-separated list (tenant:123,role:reader,env:prod)
- key_id: kms://region/keyname or hsm://serial/keyname
- key_version: string
- operation: encrypt | decrypt | sign | verify | wrap | unwrap | generate_key
- operation_context: short JSON string (max 2KB) with non-sensitive fields: request_path, model_family, sequence_length_hint
- request_id: id used across services to correlate
- latency_ms: integer string
- service_node: host id or service role
- decision_source: rbac_v2 | kms_policy | manual_approval
- justification_id: optional approval id
- audit_signature: base64(signed_digest) — used to verify record integrity when pulled into evidence store

Note: sensitive fields (full principal identity, raw request payloads, plaintext tokens) MUST NOT be shipped to SIEM. Only hashes/ids and non-sensitive context go to SIEM. Full artifacts are stored in the evidence archive with strict access controls.

SIEM mapping and ingestion guide

- Indexing: Ingest events into ecs-compliant index: log.kms_access. Use event.dataset = "kms.access" and event.module = "kms". Map outcome to event.outcome and key_id to host.id for searchability.
- ECS tags: add service.name = "redwood-kms", cloud.region, tenant.id (hashed), and deployment.mode (hosted|dedicated|private).
- Enrichment: SIEM pipeline performs geoip on service_node if external, and resolves role names from a cached mapping for dashboards.
- Parsers: implement strict JSON schema validation at ingestion to reject malformed operation_context > 2KB.

Evidence automation and forensics workflow

- Evidence package composition: for a given time window (ad-hoc or incident-driven), build a signed bundle containing: manifest.json (list of event_ids + hashes), raw secured audit blobs (signed by KMS), principal token snapshots (redacted), policy versions, and key metadata (non-secret). All bundle parts are signed by the security control plane key and checksumed.
- Chain of custody: each bundle receives a custody_id, S3 path, and retention tag. Movement between storage classes is auditable.
- Access controls: evidence retrieval requires multi-party approval (security + platform lead) and is logged to a separate immutable store.

Rotation coordination patterns

- Rotation types: soft rotation (create new key version and update metadata), hard rotation (create new key + re-encrypt persisted blobs), emergency rotation (revoke and generate new root).
- Coordination steps for tenant BYOK soft rotation: 1) Create new key version in HSM/KMS. 2) Update control-plane binding to accept new version. 3) Allow dual-use period where both versions are valid. 4) Schedule background rewrap job (best-effort) for persistent stores and update manifests when rewrap completes. 5) Revoke old version when rewrap completes and SLA window passed.
- Rotation SLOs: for soft rotations aim for 72 hours dual-use window; background rewrap throughput must be rate-limited per-tenant to avoid inference impact. Emergency rotations have a documented incident playbook with rollback steps.

Operational runbook (quick checklist)

- Daily: verify audit pipeline lag < 60s for critical events; check SIEM ingestion errors; ensure signing key rotation for audit_signature not older than 90 days.
- Weekly: reconcile key inventory vs role bindings; review any denied key operations with >10 retries.
- After rotation: validate sample decryption on a 1% tenant sample; verify evidence bundle integrity for the rotation window.

Alerting and detection examples

- High-confidence alert: repeated denied unwrap operations on a single key by different principals within 1 minute -> create P1 ticket.
- Medium: key_version used from two different regions in unrealistic pattern (compare against expected region list).
- Low: late audit records (lag > 10 minutes) for decryption operations on dedicated clusters.

Implementation notes and optimizations

- Non-blocking audit: KMS returns result immediately and emits audit event asynchronously to audit pipeline. The KMS includes a persistent event_id in response; downstream systems can query evidence store for full artifact if needed.
- Batching: for high-throughput inference, aggregate per-request low-signal telemetry (cache hits, prefix usage) into 1s batches to reduce noise in SIEM; still emit one authoritative KMS audit event per key operation.
- Token hash rotation: to preserve traceability, use stable principal_id mapping for 90 days, then rotate hash salt monthly and maintain mapping in evidence archive.

Open questions / TODOs

- Decide canonical retention tiers across customer classes (default 1 year, enterprise 3 years, eDiscovery 7 years) and add to SLA appendix.
- Define exact approval flow for evidence retrieval (UI vs API, whitelisting for EDR).
- Performance budget for background rewrap jobs on Dedicated clusters; need SRE runbook to limit IO/CPU impact.

Appendix: example SIEM query snippets

- Detect repeated denied unwraps: 
  event.dataset: "kms.access" and outcome: "denied" | stats count by key_id, principal_id | where count > 5

- One-off suspicious immediate rotation followed by access: 
  event.dataset: "kms.access" and operation: "generate_key" and timestamp > now-1h | join (event.dataset: "kms.access" operation: "decrypt" ) by request_id

- Verify signature validity for recent bundles (offline check): list bundles where manifest signature verification failed -> alert security team.

Notes for reviewers

This is an operational-first draft meant to be implementation guidance for infra, SRE, and security teams. Feedback requested on retention tiers, evidence access policy, and allowed fields in operation_context. Particularly interested in SRE input on rewrap throttling constraints.
